explanation: Mask to 64 bits, compare the selected bit values, and toggle both only when they differ. Interpret the final pattern using the displayed signed 64-bit convention, including the sign bit.
timeComplexity: O(1) time. Two bit extractions and at most one XOR mask are performed.
spaceComplexity: O(1) auxiliary space. Only fixed-width words and shift indices are stored.
attribution: Original Python implementation authored for EPI Practice from its displayed contract and independently authored C# solution; no upstream reference source adapted.
correctness: If the selected bits are equal, swapping them changes nothing. If they differ, XOR with a mask containing exactly those two positions toggles each to the other’s value while leaving every unselected bit unchanged. Reinterpreting the input as ulong makes shifts logical across all 64 positions; converting the final bit pattern back preserves its signed two’s-complement interpretation.
walkthrough: 82 has set bits at positions 6, 4 and 1. Swap positions 1 and 5: they contain 1 and 0, so XOR with 2 + 32 = 34. The resulting set positions are 6, 5 and 4, representing 64 + 32 + 16 = 112. Return 112.
edgeCases: Equal positions or equal selected bits leave the value unchanged.
Position 63 is the sign bit and must still participate in the swap.
Negative inputs are treated as full 64-bit two’s-complement bit patterns.
The input is masked to 64 bits and the output pattern is converted to signed two’s-complement form.
